subject: Conditional volume signal and pricing gate for hosted API commit
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@emberhealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@emberhealth.com
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing gating & breakpoints — need clarification

Hi Jasmine / Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — Ember team is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Before procurement drafts terms I need one clean ask: how will the per-token discount ladder behave when usage is bursty and highly seasonal for us? Specifically: 

- Do you support a conditional "volume signal" that allows discounts to materialize only after a rolling window of sustained usage (e.g., 30-day rolling average) rather than instant breakpoint crediting?
- Are your discounts calculated as marginal (per-token at each band) or blended (single rate applied to total usage)?
- What are the typical true-up triggers and cadence you recommend for enterprise customers (monthly vs quarterly)?

We're preparing a master agreement and would like concrete language to put in the volume/discount section so our legal/procurement can move forward. I've attached the draft MA for context (Ember_MA_Draft_v1.pdf).

Priority for us is: 1) predictable unit economics for forecasting, 2) protection from transient spikes causing over-discounting, and 3) a simple true-up cadence (monthly preferred).

Can you respond with a proposed gating approach and a sample schedule (bands + example pricing math) we can circulate?

Thanks,
Amit
Amit Shah
Head of Platform & Data, Ember Health

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@emberhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2028 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing gating & breakpoints — need clarification

Hi Amit — great question and thanks for sharing the MA. I pulled together a short proposal and an example workbook (attached) to make the math concrete. See attachment: Redwood_Commit_Tiers_v3.xlsx.

Summary (recommended approach):
- Signal window: use a 30-day rolling usage signal to gate breakpoint eligibility. This prevents single-day spikes from immediately unlocking lower marginal rates.
- Discount accounting: we recommend marginal discounts by default (tokens billed at the marginal rate for the band they fall into). For customers that prefer simplicity, we can optionally provide a blended invoicing view on request (blended is for reporting only; underlying accounting remains marginal).
- True-up cadence: monthly true-ups are supported and are our standard for hosted customers. Quarterly true-ups are available for larger annual-commit deals if you want fewer reconciliations.

Operational details / guardrails:
- Breakpoint lookback: each billing month we compute the 30-day rolling volume as of the last day of the month. If the rolling signal crosses a breakpoint and remains above the breakpoint threshold for 3 consecutive days, the lower marginal rate applies for the remainder of that billing month (and onward until the signal drops below breakpoint).
- Stepdown protection: a 14-day cool-down avoids flip-flop when usage hovers near a breakpoint.
- Cap on retroactive credits: we do not apply retroactive credits beyond the month in which the breakpoint was crossed to keep reconciliation tractable.

Example: if your 30-day rolling usage crosses the 10B-token band on April 10 and stays above for 3 days, tokens beyond 10B for April are billed at the lower marginal rate; any prior months are not retroactively adjusted. The workbook shows marginal vs blended examples side-by-side.

Next steps: 1) review the attached workbook with your finance team, 2) tell us whether you need a blended-only contractual representation (we can add a clause), and 3) if you want, schedule a 30-min pricing walk-through — Ben and Laura can join.

Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Amit — quick follow-up from my side with a concrete commercial suggestion to simplify negotiation:

Proposal (hybrid):
- Base blended rate for first 2B tokens/month (keeps invoice predictable).
- Marginal ladder kicks in above 2B with clear breakpoints at 5B, 10B, 25B.
- 30-day rolling signal + 3-day confirmation and 14-day cool-down as Jasmine outlined.
- Monthly true-up; we cap aggregate retroactive credits to 2% of that month's bill to limit exposure on very volatile months.

Why hybrid? Many customers want a simple baseline for forecasting (blended) but still benefit from marginal economics if they consistently scale. This structure is often easier for procurement to accept because it blends predictability and upside.

If that sounds reasonable I can model a sample with actual $/token rates and send an updated SOW snippet for legal to review (will reference EH-2028-042).

-Ben
